# Objective

- Closes #4464 

## Solution

- Specify default mag and min filter types for `Image` instead of using `wgpu`'s defaults.

---

## Changelog

### Changed

- Default `Image` filtering changed from `Nearest` to `Linear`.

I feel like linear makes more sense as a global default personally. If people want a pixellated style, I feel like that should be the exception. And then model loaders should respect the conventions of the model format. I feel like sprites could maybe prefer nearest neighbour as a default but it’s not certain. What’s your perspective on this @cart ?

Linear does seem like reasonable default. I think godot does default to linear for textures. This feels like a "defer to the ecosystem to avoid surprising people" sort of situation. Before making the change, we should sample the defaults from some popular projects.

Regardless of the choice, we should try to improve the docs here in a very visible place.

I'm tempted by the module docs for bevy_render

Trying to find defaults in the unity/unreal/godot docs has been surprisingly challenging.

- Unity - bilinear is default: https://danielilett.com/2019-09-08-unity-tips-3-interpolation/#:~:text=the%20default%20value%20for%20which%20is%20Bilinear
- Godot - some old docs suggest that "filtering" is on by default. This issue suggests linear is on by default https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/57679#issuecomment-1030712111 and nearest is opt-in. Another interesting comment here https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/59803 
> Linear filtering will not be disabled by default, as most people are not creating 2D pixel art games (and disabling filtering has adverse effects for non-pixel art games)
- Unreal - the unreal wiki suggests bilinear is default. Couldn't find an answer in the official docs.

From what I can find, it seems like the general approach is `linear` filtering by default, with a global setting in the API to enable `nearest` for 2d sprite games.

I guess then we would need a global setting resource to configure the default...? That may be a bit difficult API-wise. I feel like we could try to do it and if it becomes clear that it is too cumbersome, then we could just change it to linear and deal with the exceptions.

A related issue: do we have a good way to override the filter in a per-texture way? The only method that crosses my mind is to mess with `Assets<Image>` directly, but it is not ideal as it can only be done after the image is loaded.

@cart based on the references above, I think the best path forward is:

1. Merge this PR as-is to default to `Linear` as the option-of-least-surprise.
2. Users who need `Nearest` can still change it by editing the `Image` asset.
3. Future work should figure out how to make this easier. Does this happen during asset loading? Is the `Sampler` tied to the `Image`, or should it be set anywhere the `Image` is *used* similar to Godot?

Ultimately filters will be configured for texture assets in `.meta` files next to the textures in the asset folder. Defining project-specific override-able defaults for those `.meta` files seems like the way to go medium-to-long term. In the short term, this happens at runtime, so we might want to make it a configurable global, even though thats just a partial solution. Per-asset configuration is currently harder than it should be: @mockersf has this PR, which offers an easier middle ground solution #1665. But I'm still not convinced thats the direction we should go down (even in the short term), as it requires duplicating assets. I _am_ warming up to pragmatic short term solutions though. Some sort of simple "per-asset import post processor" or "asset import configurator" feels reasonable.
I do think I agree with @aevyrie's laid out plan for "right now" though.

I have been having a thought about samplers and whether we really need all of the samplers we currently create and bind. It looked to me like if we use the same sampler configuration for sampling all base colour textures, for example, then we only need to create one sampler for that, not one per texture. I checked this with @cwfitzgerald in #rendering-dev on Discord and it seems to be true. Indeed there are limitations on the number of samplers for some platforms (possibly max 2k on DX12 and and possibly max 2k per command buffer on Dawn were named.)
exjam, who is working on porting an actual previously-released (old?) production game to bevy using existing assets hit the sampler limit. Just to note this data point.

> I have been having a thought about samplers and whether we really need all of the samplers we currently create and bind. It looked to me like if we use the same sampler configuration for sampling all base colour textures, for example, then we only need to create one sampler for that, not one per texture. I checked this with @cwfitzgerald in #rendering-dev on Discord and it seems to be true. Indeed there are limitations on the number of samplers for some platforms (possibly max 2k on DX12 and and possibly max 2k per command buffer on Dawn were named.)

Yeah we should consider de-duplicating samplers. In practice there shouldn't be many permutations.
Are there any tasks needed to complete for this PR, or is this discussion for future sampler changes?

> @cart based on the references above, I think the best path forward is:
> 
> 1. Merge this PR as-is to default to `Linear` as the option-of-least-surprise.
> 2. Users who need `Nearest` can still change it by editing the `Image` asset.
> 3. Future work should figure out how to make this easier. Does this happen during asset loading? Is the `Sampler` tied to the `Image`, or should it be set anywhere the `Image` is _used_ similar to Godot?

I agree with this. I think we should merge this PR and change the default to Linear. Ok, @cart ?

This will graphically break `examples/2d/sprite_sheet.rs` which currently depends on nearest neighbour sampling being the default (the example displays rescaled pixel graphics, and linear sampling could also cause spritesheet bleeding). That said, the example might be a decent place to show users how to switch the sampling mode manually.

(Please correct me if I'm wrong about the spritesheet bleeding. In the past I've had minor issues with bleeding while using nearest neighbour sampling, so I'm assuming linear will cause more)

Hmm yeah given how disruptive this could be for 2d sprite workflows, I think we should have an easy / satisfactory solution in place before merging (and ensure relevant examples like sprite_sheet are updated to use it).

This blurriness definitely isn't a good look for what is probably the first example sprite-curious people will look at:
  
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2694663/170391350-35d15e3a-c582-4e6a-bed1-c905f6b7f27e.png)


I think a simple global resource to configure the default sampler is a good middle ground solution that will make existing "sprite based" workflows continue to work properly:
```rust
struct DefaultImageSampler(SamplerDescriptor<'static>);

app.insert_resource(DefaultImageSampler::linear());
```

We'd need to update Image::sampler_descriptor to have some something like:

```rust
enum ImageSampler {
  Default,
  Descriptor(SamplerDescriptor<'static>)
}
```

For `ImageSampler::Default`, we would query `DefaultImageSampler` at runtime in `<Image as RenderAsset>::prepare_asset`.

Alright, I've included `cart`s feedback here and cleaned up comments. I used feedback from @superdump on discord to use the resource extraction trait.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2632925/172466511-95023308-eba5-4a98-a143-b81656580ec2.mp4

Setting the image filter globally in the sprite sheet example:
```rs
.insert_resource(DefaultImageSampler::nearest()) // prevents blurry sprites
```

> Hmm yeah given how disruptive this could be for 2d sprite workflows, I think we should have an easy / satisfactory solution in place before merging (and ensure relevant examples like sprite_sheet are updated to use it).

I believe the "correct" way to do it would be to have support for "pixel art filtering" shader, which incidently also requries the textures to be set to linear filtering. That solves the issue with the default value, and in fact makes the pixel art games look better on screens of various densities/not aligned pixel grids.

Here's a shadertoy that shows the effect i'm talking about: https://www.shadertoy.com/view/ltBGWc

I guess in context of this PR it would be an extra argument to switch to Linear and not bother with reconfigurable defaults too much.

I do think that supporting something like that shader is a good idea. However supporting that feels like something that deserves to be solved in its own time (separate from default values), as there are a number of design questions to answer:
* Do we put the "pixel_art_filtering" switch on Sprite entity config or on image assets? This would be using specialization to set shader defs, so this will ultimately be "per entity work" no matter what. But is "pixel-art-ness" inherent to an image, or is it a choice to be made by a thing consuming an image?
* How much frame time does the extra shader work cost? Will it significantly regress things like bevymark?
*  Should sprites use the "pixel_art" shader by default?

I don't think "global default filtering settings" are particularly harmful (and seem like a useful tool). Long term, I suspect we'd move this sort of thing into the asset processing system (.meta files and maybe global defaults for the configuration in them).

Pixel art filtering would still almost certainly be opt-in (and might also need a global default), so I don't think it would meaningfully change the user experience / code patterns here (relative to setting a global Nearest filter).
In that case, I think everything here is good, pending one last look-over.

Just pushed one minor tweak (for your consideration). I split out the default sampler config into a new `ImageSettings` struct. I think thats a bit more idiomatic, and it also separates the concern of "configuration" from "runtime value", which allows us to remove the `Option<Sampler>` and the resource extraction. And it also removes the need to pass in a render_device to read the sampler. Instead, we just generate the DefaultImageSampler (with a Sampler) once at startup.
Makes sense to me. :+1:

issue_context.title: Default `Image` filtering `Nearest` causes artifacts
issue_context.body:
## What you did

Scaled an image in bevy_egui, resulting in aliasing artifacts. See https://github.com/mvlabat/bevy_egui/issues/89

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2632925/163076001-c01f7969-97a3-4011-b1fe-828a6916dca5.png)

## What you expected to happen

I would expect images to default to linear filtering.

## What actually happened

Bevy appears to default `Image`s' `SamplerDescriptor` to `Nearest`, because it is wgpu's default:

### Bevy:
https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/0529f633f9e6f4633b9f2c54fb99ef99427d1ec5/crates/bevy_render/src/texture/image.rs#L134

### wgpu `SamplerDescriptor`:
https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/blob/e4553d7e169a6edf1a4f1b2a983b96700fa098f2/wgpu-core/src/resource.rs#L469-L471

### wgpu `FilterMode`:
https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/blob/988990c24d0933c82cdd661708a3f5bcb4533ea3/wgpu-types/src/lib.rs#L3203

review_comments: Docs please <3 This definitely needs to link to `DefaultImageSampler`.
